name: Italian Game
intro: The Italian Game develops quickly, points the bishop at Black's weak f7-square, and fights for the center. It leads to both quiet positional play (Giuoco Pianissimo) and sharp lines.

line.comment: Stake a claim in the center and open lines for the bishop and queen.
Black mirrors, contesting the center directly.
Develop with a threat: the knight attacks the e5-pawn.
Defend e5 and develop toward the center.

alts.comment: The Petrov Defense — Black counterattacks e4 instead of defending e5. A different opening entirely.

line.comment: The move that names the opening: the bishop eyes f7, the weakest square in Black's camp.

alts.comment: The Ruy Lopez — pinning pressure on the c6-knight instead.

line.comment: The Giuoco Piano ('quiet game'): Black mirrors, aiming the bishop at f2.

alts.comment: The Two Knights Defense — a sharper, more aggressive try that invites tactics.

line.comment: Prepare d4, building a big center. The modern main line often continues with slow maneuvering (the Giuoco Pianissimo).
The Giuoco Pianissimo: support e4 and keep the center closed for slow, strategic play.
